spans.text: Devas are the angelic champions who fight on behalf of the gods. They are angelic in appearance, with bodies that are either abstract and mystifying or the epitome of a human’s perception of beauty. They are created from the influence of a god to act in their place where it is necessary, often as a divine messenger or a righteous warrior. Devas can be elevated from petitioners or particularly dogmatic mortals, but the transformation results in an angel that is no longer simply what it was. Devas can be found across the planes for a variety of purposes: they may be dispatched by their gods for any number of reasons, summoned by particularly powerful devotees of a god, or bound to a location to serve a specific eternal purpose.
In Somnus Domina, the form of devas varies. While many exist who are traditional angels, those created from or for the Eidolons have distinct characteristics.
Deva Orders.
Devas are split into three primary orders: astral, monadic and movanic.

The strongest of them are the astral devas, who were most often sent to battle with fiends and aberrant beings, particularly in the lower planes and Astral Plane. They are the furthest from mankind, often having bodies that are abstract and difficult to comprehend compared to others. They are integral for keeping an eye on entities who wander between realms.

Monadic devas serve as personal agents, stewards, and guardians more often than not and are the most patient of the orders. They act within the Material Plane and Elemental Planes, as well as protect the upper planes from being invaded or entered without permission. They are the most common deva to offer their power as patrons to mortals who might require their aid.

Movanic devas are the weakest of the orders, but thanks to their status as similar to mankind, they are the most numerous. When a petitioner felt they had reached a point of satisfaction with their lives, they might request to give their existence up to become a movanic deva - removing themselves from the cycle of reincarnation unless that deva is vanquished or relieved of duty. They deal with matters in the Prime Material Plane and Energy Planes chiefly, and if they serve diligently they may be promoted to a monadic deva.
Domain Awareness.

When granted a connection to it, a deva gains the same awareness of all events pertaining to a domain granted by their creator, which is a domain they would share. The Eidolons deal in many domains, so they often have a deva assigned to each to keep a particularly close eye on it and grant it the attention it deserves. A deva will not take action against or involving mankind or mortal society unless directly commanded to by their god.
True or Fallen.

Even when in the service of a neutral or evil god, devas are lawful and good from conception. Devas can alter in alignment, but any deva that turns to evil (often for reasons they would seek to justify as necessary) will surely find themselves becoming fallen, losing the protection of their deities and being cast from their heavenly planes. Fallen devas sometimes become fiends or yokai, but sometimes continue to act in the way they believe their god requires of them, performing evil actions it believes are in service of the greater good.
All devas have the following traits and properties.
Angelic Weapons.
A deva’s weapon attacks are magical. When they hit with any weapon it deals an extra 4d8 radiant damage (included in their stat blocks).
Divine Judgement.

When speaking with a mortal creature, a deva can divine the crimes committed during the mortal’s life and the context surrounding them, which the deva knows with great familiarity. A being may be able to resist this effect if protected by another higher being, such as a fiend or yokai.
Deva Shapechanging.

Devas, as a bonus action, can polymorph into a humanoid of any description, a beast of a challenge rating no higher than its own, or back to its true form. If it dies, it reverts to its true form. In any humanoid form its statistics remain the same, but in the form of a beast it assumes the AC, movement, Strength, Dexterity, senses, attacks, and actions of the form (except class features, Legendary Actions, and lair actions), but keeps access to its own actions and senses as well.

All devas hold a distaste for unnecessary armor and clothes, as they hold the belief that their natural bodies are a symbol of their divinity, so they often appear unclothed or close to it. They do not allow this to get in the way of appearing in whatever form they must to appear in the Material Plane or to perform whatever tasks they are charged with.
Deva Properties.
Devas all have the following general properties:

bullets.text: Devas do not require air, food or water and are immune to the effects of the inner planes and extreme environmental effects - astral devas are also resistant to the effects of the lower planes, where they are often dispatched.
Their maximum hit points cannot be reduced.

If they die in the inner planes, their body and possessions vanish in a flash of light and reform 10 years later in their native plane. If destroyed on any other plane they are vanquished permanently. A vanquished deva’s memories and critical knowledge returns to a living deva of their faith who they were closest to.
They cannot be surprised in combat, even if caught unaware.
